message.content:
In poker there’s no “special” player who automatically ends up with more hearts than everyone else – hearts are just one of the four suits, and the number a player holds is entirely determined by the deal.

**So the maximum number of hearts a player can have is simply the number of cards dealt to them in that particular game.**

| Game type | Cards per player | Max hearts a single player can hold |
|-----------|------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Texas Hold’em (standard) | 2 | 2 |
| Five‑Card Draw | 5 | 5 |
| Seven‑Card Stud | 7 | 7 |
| Omaha (4‑card hand) | 4 | 4 |
| Razz (5‑card hand) | 5 | 5 |

If you’re playing a variant where each player gets, say, 8 cards, then the theoretical maximum hearts would be 8, and so on. There’s no rule that gives one player more hearts than another; it’s purely random.

If you’d like to see a concrete example, just let me know how many players and how many cards per player you want, and I can deal a hand for you and count the hearts.
